dek: The Machine's Picks sells memberships from a $99 day pass to $5,895 for two years and advertises 15 straight profitable years at a 62.3% win rate. Buyer reviews are few, mostly positive and short term.

short_answer: The Machine's Picks is a real, long running business. It names a company, Machines Picks Inc., publishes a full price list and written refund terms, and has customer reviews under the same name going back to 2014. Picks go out by text or email before games, and the site says 2026 results are posted daily on its X page. It does not name the person or people who make the picks, and it gives no address or phone number.

Whether its picks make money is much harder to answer. The headline numbers, 10,116-6,134, 62.3% and +22,635 units since 2011, come from the seller's own yearly tables. We added those tables up and they are internally consistent, but the site says itself that 2011 to 2025 is shown as yearly totals, not a pick by pick log, and its FAQ says no third party tracks it. The one detailed log it offers is a three month sample it chose, Q1 2026, with dates but no send times, and that quarter ran well above its own long term average.

Treat it as an established seller with an unproven record and high prices. If you buy, start short, log every pick with the line you actually got and the units risked, and judge it after a few hundred picks rather than one streak. There is no refund for losing picks.

guarantee: There is no performance guarantee. The packages page says "All sales are final except where required by applicable law or as expressly provided in our Terms of Service." Section 09 of the terms is headed "All Sales Are Final, Except as Required by Law", says "purchases are final once payment is accepted and access to the purchased service begins", and says "Members are not entitled to refunds solely because of losing selections, unfavorable betting results". The FAQ adds that no wins are guaranteed and that losing stretches are normal.

The terms do promise a remedy for delivery problems: if picks fail to arrive, the company says it may respond by "restoring access, correcting delivery problems, extending available access, or issuing an appropriate refund." That covers service failures, not losing bets. If a card payment is disputed, the terms say access may be suspended and, if the payment is reversed, terminated. We found no auto renewal wording: the passes run for fixed periods. The terms name no governing state and no address.

claims_note: We checked the yearly table ourselves. The fifteen yearly win and loss counts add to 10,116 and 6,134, which is 62.25%, and the units add to +22,635, so the headline is consistent with the page. The 2021 to 2025 units add to +7,840.03, as the About page says. The football page also adds up: NFL 1,259-756 (+4,094.67 units) and college football 1,068-642 (+3,221.74 units), with every one of 30 football seasons profitable and the worst, NFL 2020, at 79-58 (57.7%). Consistent arithmetic shows the tables were built with care. It does not show that the picks were sent before the games, at the lines listed.

The yearly totals are unusually smooth. Every one of 15 seasons lands between +1,134 and +1,676 units, and every season's win rate sits between 61.1% and 64.4%, even though the number of picks per year ranges from 897 (2022) to 1,467 (2012). Real betting results usually swing much more. That does not prove anything is wrong, but it is a reason to ask for the picks behind the totals.

The unit totals imply large bets. +22,635 units over 16,250 picks is about +1.39 units a pick. A flat one unit bettor winning 62.3% at -110 makes about 0.19 units a pick, so the totals only work if the average play risks about seven units. That fits the Q1 sample, where 127 of 242 plays were 10 units and 101 were 5 units. It also means one losing 10 unit play at -150 costs 15 units, which is what the 14 Mar 2026 Harvard moneyline loss cost.

A three month sample picked by the seller says little about a full year. Q1 2026 at 159-76 is 67.7%, above every full season in the seller's own table. The free pick figures also move between sources: 48-18 in a 2022 article, 62% "over the last 2 years" in 2024, 644-377 on the homepage on 7 Nov 2026, and no free play record on the homepage on 20 Nov 2026.
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for The Machine's Picks plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found 264 posts naming The Machine's Picks, but none carried a play we could match to a game and grade.

What a buyer can check outside the seller: nothing independent. The FAQ says the service is not monitored by a third party tracker. We found no contest result, regulator record or tracking site for The Machine's Picks, and the Better Business Bureau search returned no results.

What the seller publishes: yearly records by sport for 2011 to 2025 with a downloadable CSV of those totals; football and basketball pages that break the same totals down by season; and a pick by pick table for 1 Jan to 31 Mar 2026 showing date, selection, line, odds, unit rating and result, with no time each pick was sent. In that sample odds run from about -105 to -155 on sides and totals, with a few long shot futures and props at +180 to +850. The five biggest losses were all 10 unit plays costing 13.9 to 15 units each. The record page says futures are counted in the year they settle and that 2026 results will be added after year end; the site says current releases are posted daily on X.
We found no court or regulator action involving The Machine's Picks or Machines Picks Inc. in our searches.

customers_intro: Customer evidence on The Machine's Picks spans 2014 to 2026 but is small: 19 Trustpilot reviews on an unclaimed profile and a handful on CapperTek. Most are positive and describe short runs or single big plays. The seller quotes several of these reviews on its own site. We found no forum thread about the service on Reddit, Sportsbook Review, TheRX or Covers. Below is everything we read and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We read 19 Trustpilot reviews dated 2018 to 2026 and the CapperTek reviews dated 2014 to 2026. Fifteen of the Trustpilot reviews are five star. The positive posts repeat the same points: the service is seen as honest about losses, members report win rates of 63% to 66% over a few months, and big rated "hammer" plays come in. Most are short and none attaches a log. The negative posts are fewer but spread over years: a 2018 buyer said they won 39% in their first month after being told 70%, a 2022 CapperTek buyer said a week of cancel emails went unanswered, a 2025 reviewer doubted the win rate and called the service a scam, a 2026 reviewer said the price is far too high, and a 2026 CapperTek reviewer said the free picks went about one or two for twelve weeks. Trustpilot notes the company has not invited reviews and that only 4 came in the last 12 months. The seller quotes several five star reviews on its own pages. We found no thread about this service on Reddit, Sportsbook Review, TheRX or Covers, and no BBB profile, so there is no wide pattern either way. Our Reddit check was partial: the Arctic Shift full text search timed out on 20 Nov 2026, and our saved library of betting subreddit posts held no mention of the service, only the seller's own X posts.

Trustpilot showed 19 reviews and a 4.2 score, 79% five star, 5% three star, 5% two star and 11% one star, on an unclaimed profile, with only 4 reviews in the last 12 months. Trustpilot says the company has not invited customers to review it.

A CapperTek reviewer said they see ads for the service constantly on social media, found the price a bit high, and tracked the free picks for about twelve weeks with only one or two wins. They also said they did not remember the older reviews and wondered whether dates could be faked. These are their claims.
A Trustpilot reviewer said they had tried about a dozen pick services and that this one is more honest about its record and avoids outrageous claims.
A Trustpilot reviewer said the visible record is what they value and reported profits over several years. No figures or log were given. The proof page summarizes a review from the same month.
A two star Trustpilot reviewer called the service decent but said the prices are far too expensive.
A Trustpilot reviewer who said they have followed several seasons praised the service as honest with no hidden losses. The seller quotes this review on its homepage, packages page and proof page.
A Trustpilot reviewer said this was the first service whose results matched its marketing. The seller summarizes a review from this month on its proof page.
A Trustpilot review marked verified said the win rate had been great, though the number of plays was lower than the reviewer wanted.

A verified Trustpilot reviewer said they were hitting about 66% on the 2025 baseball picks. A CapperTek review the day before reported 56 wins and 29 losses and $2,436 in profit for a new member. Both are self reported.

A one star Trustpilot reviewer called the service a scam, saying it would not offer free picks to monitor and that nobody hits 64%. This is the reviewer's claim; the FAQ now says free plays are offered regularly.

A Trustpilot reviewer reported more than 400 units of profit after three months. Another, in Feb 2020, described themselves as a long term member with steady yearly profits and advised careful bankroll management.

A CapperTek reviewer said they had emailed for over a week trying to cancel their service without a response. (Read on 7 Nov 2026; on 20 Nov 2026 the part of the CapperTek page that loaded showed only the three newest reviews.)
A one star Trustpilot reviewer said they were told the service wins 70% and that they won 39% after one month.

Most CapperTek reviews we read on 7 Nov 2026 were positive and described streaks or big rated plays: 26-4 in 2014, 18 straight winning days in KBO in 2020, a 3 for 3 day pass in Feb 2024, and 56-29 in 2025. A 2014 reviewer noted that picks were sent hours before games and posted on the website after the game started.

The Better Business Bureau search returned no results for Machines Picks. Web searches found no Reddit, TheRX, Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about this service; older SBR posts under a "Machine" name appear to be a different handicapper. The press pieces it links (USA Wire, Silicon Valley Times, TechBullion) contain no buyer accounts.

conflicts: The site grades its own picks and also sells them. The yearly totals, the Q1 sample, the football and basketball pages and the free play figures are all published by the seller, and the FAQ confirms there is no third party tracker.

The "Featured in Publications" logos are presented as coverage. The pieces we opened read as promotion: USA Wire (2022) is credited to "USA Wire Staff" and repeats the seller's figures, Silicon Valley Times (2024) has no named writer and ends with a call to visit the site, and the TechBullion piece (2026) gives no figures and no independent sources. The Benzinga link points to Benzinga's press release section, which normally carries material a company submits itself. Two other linked pages refused to load for us.
The seller does not say who makes the picks. The About page says the formula is "proprietary" and that the nickname came from followers, and no person is named anywhere we looked.
We saw no sportsbook affiliate links or promo codes on the pages we opened.
strengths: A named company, a full price list from a $99 day pass up, and written refund and delivery terms.
A pick by pick sample for Q1 2026 with line, odds, units and result, losses and pushes included, plus a CSV of the yearly totals.
The published tables are internally consistent: yearly records, sport pages and five year totals all add up.
Reviews under the same name go back to 2014, so the business has a long public history.
Practical FAQ advice on bankroll and unit sizing, including that a unit is not a fixed share of a bankroll and that some days have no plays.
concerns: No pick log for 2011 to 2025, no send times in the Q1 sample, and no third party tracking. The 15 year record cannot be checked pick by pick.
The yearly totals are unusually smooth, every season +1,134 to +1,676 units and 61.1% to 64.4%.
High prices: $795 a month and $3,995 a year. All sales final, and no refund for losing picks.
Large unit sizes: most plays are 5 or 10 units, so one losing 10 unit favorite can erase several smaller wins.
No named handicapper, address or phone number; contact is one email address.
"Featured in" press logos lead to promotional or submitted pieces, not independent reporting.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds, the units and the time it was sent. Yearly totals and a chosen quarter are not a record.
Count units, not wins. At 5 and 10 unit plays on favorites, a 60% record can still lose money.
Start with the 1 Day or 3 Day pass and compare the line you can actually get with the line listed.
Save your receipt and checkout email; the terms only offer remedies for delivery problems, not results.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
faq: It is a real business, Machines Picks Inc., with published prices, refund terms and customer reviews under the same name since 2014. We could not verify its long term record, because it publishes yearly totals rather than a log of every pick and says no third party tracks it. We found no court or regulator action involving it.
How much does The Machine's Picks cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 passes were $99 for a day, $199 for three days, $275 for Thursday to Sunday, $395 a week, $795 a month, $2,895 for six months, $3,995 a year and $5,895 for two years. Season passes ran from $1,099 (NFL or college football) to $1,999 (NBA plus college basketball), and an MLB playoffs pass was $449.
Does The Machine's Picks have a verified record?

No. The 62.3% and +22,635 unit figures come from the seller's own yearly tables. We checked that they add up, and they do, but the only individual picks shown are a seller chosen Q1 2026 sample without send times, and Watchdog has no graded record for it.
Can I get a refund from The Machine's Picks?

Not for losing picks. The terms say purchases are final once payment is accepted and access begins. If picks fail to arrive, the company says it may restore access, fix delivery, extend access or issue a refund.
What do buyers say about The Machine's Picks?

Mostly positive but thin: 19 Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.2 and a handful on CapperTek, many describing short winning runs. Complaints mention high prices, a poor first month, slow cancellation replies and doubts about the win rate. We found no forum discussion of it on Reddit, SBR, TheRX or Covers.
Is The Machine's Picks worth it?

For the money you get every official pick across active sports by text or email for the length you buy. What is unproven is whether a buyer, getting the line available at release, beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over time after paying $795 a month or more, and there is no refund if the picks lose.
